activities.caption: put coal's carbon bill on the scale
activities.name: esgCoalPlace

config.prompt: Lifecycle emissions, grams of CO₂ per kilowatt-hour — where does coal sit?
config.why: Coal ~820 gCO₂/kWh; gas ~490; solar ~40; wind and nuclear ~12. The transition is, in essence, moving the grid down this column while holding energy density and capacity factor steady.

activities.anchor: buried faster than it could decay
activities.caption: rebuild the coal ladder, rawest first
activities.name: esgCoalRankOrder

config.prompt: Heat and pressure upgrade buried peat — put the ranks in order, rawest first:
config.why: Each step drives off water and volatiles, raising carbon content and energy density — from the swampy Carboniferous forests of about 300 million years ago, the era that named the fuel.

activities.anchor: The mitigation end of the extraction story
activities.caption: find the faulty line — the fracking briefing
activities.name: esgFrackSpot

config.prompt: A briefing on fracking's risk record contains one faulty line — click it:
lines: Fracking pumps water, sand and chemicals at pressures that crack the shale and hold the cracks open.
Methane leakage matters: methane is ~30× CO₂'s warming power over a century, so leaks can erase gas's climate advantage.
The induced earthquakes in Oklahoma were driven mostly by fracking of the production wells themselves.
Local water stress is one of the documented problems.
The renewables-and-batteries pathway is also extractive — copper, lithium, cobalt, nickel and rare earths.
config.correction: The Oklahoma earthquakes were driven mostly by wastewater injection — pumping the spent fluid back down — a narrower risk record than fracking's reputation.
config.why: The documented problems are methane leakage, induced seismicity tied to wastewater disposal, and local water stress — real, but specific.

activities.caption: the control desk — frequency is sagging
activities.name: esgGridBranch

config.root: You are on the control desk of a national grid. It is a cold, still evening and demand is climbing fast.

start.text: Demand has outrun your forecast: generation now trails draw and system frequency begins to sag. First move?

choices.label: Call on balancing services — reserve that responds in seconds
choices.feedback: That is what the auction buys: seconds-fast response holds the line while slower plant spins up.

choices.label: Do nothing — frequency will recover on its own
choices.feedback: It will not self-correct: the sag deepens until protection steps in.

choices.label: Order the wind fleet to produce more
choices.feedback: The evening is still — the fuel arrives when the weather sends it, and tonight it is not sending any.

reserve.text: Frequency stabilises. Tomorrow's auction prices the lesson in: demand forecasting (weather-driven, literally), plant scheduling, and reserve paid to respond in seconds.

drift.text: Draw keeps exceeding generation; drift too far and protection systems disconnect generators to save the hardware — the cascade that blacked out 50 million people in 2003.

wind.text: The redesign manages timing instead of assuming always-on supply: storage, demand response, interconnection over wide areas — wind is always blowing somewhere, just not here.

config.why: A grid has almost no storage: supply must equal demand every second, and frequency is the tell.

activities.caption: bet before you read on — the windless week
activities.name: esgLullPredict

config.q: A high-pressure system calms the wind over an entire region for a week. What does that do to the claim that renewables cannot run a modern grid?
choices: Settles it — a week without wind ends the experiment
It sharpens the real question: correlated lulls are the genuine challenge, and they are solvable at a price of firmness that keeps falling
It only matters for small islands
config.why: Individual windless nights are trivial; the real test is correlated lulls and seasonal balance — met with storage, interconnection, demand flexibility and forecasting, as the price of firmness keeps dropping.

activities.anchor: The transition's economics flipped within one decade
activities.caption: call the price collapse — the solar curve
activities.name: esgSolarEstimate

config.prompt: Solar module prices fell about 90% from 2010 to 2020. In 2020, a module cost roughly what fraction of its 2010 price?
config.why: About a tenth of the 2010 price — a learning rate near 20% per doubling of capacity, the steepest cost curve of any energy technology ever measured.
config.context: Onshore wind fell by about two-thirds over the same decade; batteries dropped about 90% from 2010 to 2023.

activities.anchor: Efficiency is the resource nobody builds and everybody saves
activities.caption: pair each demand-side lever with its mechanism
activities.name: esgEfficiencyMatch

config.prompt: Five levers for bending the demand curve — pair each with how it works:

pairs.right: insulation is permanent savings on the largest building loads — heating and cooling
LED lighting cut lighting's electricity demand roughly in half in a decade
time-of-use pricing shifts load into sunny hours — the grid's free storage
delivers three to four units of heat per unit of electricity by moving heat rather than making it

config.why: Every avoided kilowatt-hour avoids the generation, transmission and emissions attached to it — conservation buys the time that storage and transmission need to mature.

activities.caption: true or false — the heat-pump accounting
activities.name: esgHeatPumpJudge

statements.s: A heat pump delivering three to four units of heat per unit of electricity violates thermodynamics.
statements.why: It moves existing heat rather than making it — the honest figure of merit is the coefficient of performance.

statements.s: A furnace loses part of its energy up the flue.
statements.why: Burning fuel makes heat and part of it escapes as exhaust — a heat pump instead pumps heat up a modest temperature gradient.

statements.s: A heat pump can deliver more heat energy than the electricity it consumes.
statements.why: A 300–400% figure of merit that is honest accounting, not a perpetual-motion claim.

statements.s: Heat-pump performance should be read as a conversion efficiency, like a power plant's.
statements.why: Coefficient of performance, not conversion efficiency — the two numbers answer different questions.
